subtitle: דלאלהֵ אלחאירין — The Guide of the Perplexed
author: Moses Maimonides (1138–1204)
intro: Male ('full / to fill') is equivocal: of one body filling another ('and she filled her pitcher'); of a span of time being completed ('and her days were fulfilled'); and of perfection and the utmost degree of an excellence ('full of the blessing of the Lord'). 'The whole earth is full of His glory' (Isa 6:3) means the whole earth bears witness to His perfection — not that any body fills a place. Hover a phrase to see its English light up; tap any word for a gloss; dotted words are key terms.

terms.note: Equivocal: (1) one body filling another, (2) the completing of a measured span of time, (3) perfection and the utmost degree of an excellence.
The third sense: 'He filled them with wisdom of heart' (Exod 35:35) — being perfect and at the highest degree of a virtue.
How 'the whole earth is full of His glory' is to be read: the whole earth testifies to and points to His perfection — not a body filling a place.
Alternatively one may take 'the glory of the Lord' as the created light everywhere called kavod — and it was this that 'filled the tabernacle' — and there is no harm in that.

aligned.ja: אלג'ז אלאול · אלפצל אלתאסע עשר — מלא
מלא הד'א אסם משתרך. יסתעמלה אהל אללגה פי ג'סם יחל פי ג'סם פימלאה: ותמלא כדה, מלא העומר לאחד. והד'א כת'יר.
aligned.en: Male is an equivocal noun. The masters of the language use it of a body that lodges within a body and fills it: 'and she filled her pitcher' (Gen 24:16); 'the omer-full for each' (Exod 16:33). And this is frequent.

pairs.en: Male is an equivocal noun

aligned.ja: ויסתעמל פי מעני אנקצ'א זמאן מא מקדר ותמאמה: וימלאו ימיה, וימלאו לו ארבעים יום.
aligned.en: And it is used in the sense of the elapsing of some measured span of time and its completion: 'and her days were fulfilled' (Gen 25:24); 'and forty days were fulfilled for him' (Gen 50:3).

pairs.ja: ויסתעמל פי מעני אנקצ'א זמאן מא מקדר ותמאמה
pairs.en: And it is used in the sense of the elapsing of some measured span of time and its completion
and her days were fulfilled
and forty days were fulfilled for him

aligned.ja: ויסתעמל פי מעני אלכמאל פי אלפצ'ילה ואלגאיה פיהא: ומלא ברכת י״י, מלא אותם חכמת לב, וימלא את החכמה ואת התבונה ואת הדעת.
aligned.en: And it is used in the sense of perfection in an excellence and the utmost degree of it: 'full of the blessing of the Lord' (Deut 33:23); 'He hath filled them with wisdom of heart' (Exod 35:35); 'and He filled him with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge' (Exod 31:3).

He hath filled them with wisdom of heart

pairs.en: and He filled him with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge

aligned.ja: ומן הד'א אלמעני קיל: מלא כל הארץ כבודו — מענאה ג'מיע אלארץ' תשהד בכמאלה, אי תדל עליה. וכד'לך קולה: וכבוד י״י מלא את המשכן.
aligned.en: And of this sense it is said: 'the whole earth is full of His glory' (Isa 6:3) — its meaning is that all the earth bears witness to His perfection, that is, points to Him. And likewise His saying: 'and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle' (Exod 40:34).

pairs.en: And of this sense it is said
the whole earth is full of His glory

pairs.ja: מענאה ג'מיע אלארץ' תשהד בכמאלה, אי תדל עליה

And likewise His saying

aligned.ja: וכל לשון מליאה תג'דהא מנסובה ללה פהי מן הד'א אלמעני, לא אן ת'ם ג'סם ימלא מכאנא. אלא אן תריד תג'על כבוד י״י אלנור אלמכ'לוק אלד'י יסמי כבוד פי כל מוצ'ע, והו אלד'י מלא את המשכן, פלא צ'יר פי ד'לך.
aligned.en: And every expression of 'filling' that you find ascribed to God is of this sense — not that there is a body that fills a place. Unless you wish to take 'the glory of the Lord' as the created light that is everywhere called kavod, and it was this that 'filled the tabernacle': there is no harm in that.
